label: Lord of all: a primitive predicate for dominion over everything else
definition: PRIMITIVE. IsLord g: g has dominion over everything else, i.e. authority to dispose of it as subject to g. After ST I q.13 a.7, where 'Lord' is said of God relative to creatures, which are subject to him. Example: an owner of a field, with respect to the field (a limited dominion). Counterexample: a cause whose effect is not subject to its disposal (a parent of an adult, in the respect in which the adult is independent).
note: Explicitly identified primitive (Encode first). Open semantic obligation: a typed account of dominion (subjection, authority to dispose) that would let the bridge from causing the being of all to lordship be derived or fail. The only constraint placed on it is the open bridge 'Whatever causes the being of everything else is lord of everything else'.
